clue.text: Celebrated fellow introducing prophetic work about university

indicators.note: the fellow comes first and so introduces what follows
the prophetic book is wrapped around the university letter

parts.note: Amos is a book of the Old Testament prophets

explanation.surface: A famous man presents a scholarly study of prophecy concerning a university.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone celebrated is widely known and acclaimed, which is a straight synonym.

clue.text: Top-quality light installed in tree

indicators.note: the match is placed inside the tree word

parts.note: the fir is a coniferous tree
a vesta is a short match, something that gives light

explanation.surface: A top-grade lamp is fitted into a tree, like a Christmas decoration.
explanation.walkthrough: A vesta is an old word for a wax match.
explanation.definitionFit: Five-star describes the highest grade, as in hotel ratings.

clue.text: Break norm, e.g. on length, unlike well-bred setter, say

indicators.note: the length letter is placed on after the anagram
the letters are broken up and rearranged

parts.note: the letters of these words are used as written, as the fodder

explanation.surface: A rule is broken over length, unlike the conduct of a well-bred setter.
explanation.walkthrough: The setter here is a dog breed, not the puzzle's compiler.
explanation.definitionFit: A mongrel is a dog of mixed breed, the opposite of a pedigree setter.

clue.text: Ubiquitous shift in values? That's about right

indicators.note: the rearranged letters go around the right letter
the letters of the two words shift into a new arrangement

parts.note: the letters of these two words are used as written, as the fodder

explanation.surface: A change in values everywhere, and that is surely right.
explanation.definitionFit: Universal means found everywhere, just as ubiquitous does.

clue.text: Addict losing head with bad habits, hence court actions

indicators.note: the word for an addict drops its first letter

parts.note: a drug user is an addict
vices are bad habits

explanation.surface: An addict sinks into bad habits and ends up facing legal proceedings in court.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Court actions' suggests lawsuits, but the court is a tennis court.
explanation.definitionFit: In tennis, each serve that starts a point is a service, so these are strokes played on court.

clue.text: European with brief lecture that is about one group engaged in politics

indicators.note: the lecture word is cut short to its first four letters

parts.note: taken as written before it is cut short

indicators.note: the abbreviation for that is goes around the word for one

parts.note: i.e. abbreviates id est, that is
taken as written, the word itself
a ring is a group, as of conspirators

explanation.surface: A European gives a short talk about a group's role in politics.
explanation.definitionFit: Electioneering is campaigning to win votes, the activity of those engaged in politics at election time.

clue.text: Critical volume on EU country abridged

indicators.note: the volume letter sits on top of the shortened country
the country's name loses its final letter

parts.note: Italy is a member of the European Union

explanation.surface: A critical book about an EU member state appears in abridged form.
explanation.definitionFit: Vital means essential or of critical importance.

clue.text: Cut line holding a Spanish ship

indicators.note: the cut-and-line letters hold the single letter inside

parts.note: to carve is to cut
taken as written, the letter itself

explanation.surface: Someone cuts a rope to hold a Spanish vessel.
explanation.definitionFit: A caravel was a light sailing ship used by Spanish and Portuguese explorers.

clue.text: Possibly hiding-place for ace record-holder

definitions.meaning: a card cheat keeps an ace up his ...
a vinyl record is kept in a cardboard ...

explanation.walkthrough: 'Record-holder' sounds like a champion, but it means the cover of a gramophone record.
explanation.definitionFit: The part of a garment covering the arm can hide a card, and a disc's protective cover shares the name.

clue.text: Awfully ill, appreciates incomplete coverage — seen as ominous by some

definitions.text: incomplete coverage — seen as ominous by some

indicators.note: the letters are put together awfully, in a jumbled order

parts.note: the letters of these words are used as written, as the fodder

explanation.surface: A sick person values partial insurance, which some regard as a bad sign.
explanation.definitionFit: When the moon covers only part of the sun, the event has long been taken as a bad omen.

clue.text: Deflect criticism from very short show

parts.note: very is shortened to its abbreviation
to indicate is to show

explanation.surface: Someone escapes criticism by putting on a brief performance.
explanation.definitionFit: To vindicate someone is to clear them of blame, turning criticism away from them.

clue.text: Using few words repeatedly included by better setters, etc

indicators.note: the answer sits inside the words twice over, once spanning the first two words and once the last two
the answer is contained within the run of clue words

parts.note: the answer runs across the word break in these words, as written

explanation.surface: A boast that good crossword setters and their kind use few words.
explanation.walkthrough: It can be found in 'better setters' and again in 'setters, etc', hence 'repeatedly'.
explanation.definitionFit: Terse describes speech or writing that is brief and to the point, sparing in words.

clue.text: Search Internet link the wrong way, in excess

parts.note: to surf is to browse the web

indicators.note: the link word is written backwards

parts.note: a tie is a link or bond

explanation.surface: Browsing online and following a link backwards leads to far too much.
explanation.definitionFit: A surfeit is an excessive amount, an oversupply of something.

clue.text: Before four, servant returns in Mediterranean city

indicators.note: the reversed servant word goes in front of the number
the servant word is read backwards

parts.note: a valet is a personal manservant
IV is four in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: A servant comes back to a Mediterranean city before four o'clock.
explanation.definitionFit: Tel Aviv is the major Israeli city on the Mediterranean coast.

clue.text: Finally shortened book of world records?

indicators.note: the phrase loses its final letter

parts.note: 'at last' means finally

explanation.surface: At last a shortened edition of a book of world records appears.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Book of world records' hints at the Guinness book, but the records here are maps of the world.
explanation.definitionFit: An atlas is a bound collection of maps, recording the geography of the world.

clue.text: Charming article on the cards about Queen

indicators.note: the possible word goes around the queen's letter

parts.note: something on the cards is possible, so doable

explanation.surface: A charming item on a fortune-teller's cards is said to concern the Queen.
explanation.definitionFit: Adorable means delightful and lovable, a near synonym for charming.

clue.text: Exploit commercial opening on Northern river

indicators.note: the earlier pieces sit on the river

parts.note: an ad is a commercial
a vent is an opening
the Ure is a river in North Yorkshire

explanation.surface: A firm takes advantage of a business opening by a river in the north.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Exploit' is a noun here, a daring deed, not the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: An exploit is a bold or daring feat, which is what an adventure is.

clue.text: Accommodation over club that's no longer a pressing requirement

definitions.text: that's no longer a pressing requirement

indicators.note: in a down clue the accommodation word sits over the club word

parts.note: a flat is an apartment
an iron is a golf club

explanation.surface: Living over a golf club is no longer an urgent need.
explanation.definitionFit: A flatiron was an old heated iron for pressing clothes, now superseded by electric ones.

clue.text: It enables speculator to see what's central to board

definitions.meaning: read cryptically: a bull is a speculator betting on rising prices

explanation.walkthrough: A bull on the stock market is a speculator who expects prices to rise; his eye is literally the bull's eye.
explanation.definitionFit: The bullseye is the small target ring at the middle of a dartboard, worth the most points.

clue.text: Instrument filled with water falling in part of USSR once

indicators.note: the instrument word has the water word put inside it

parts.note: a uke is a ukulele
rain is water falling from the sky

explanation.surface: A musical instrument is left out in the rain in a former Soviet region.
explanation.definitionFit: Ukraine was a Soviet republic until independence in 1991.

clue.text: Possibly a solemn promise by English learner

definitions.note: the letter A is one example of the class, so the definition names an instance

indicators.note: the English and learner letters are placed by, next to, the promise word

parts.note: a vow is a solemn promise

explanation.surface: An English learner perhaps makes a solemn pledge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a' looks like an article, but it is the letter A, one example of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: The letter A is one of the five vowels of the alphabet, so it is an example.

clue.text: Why I get confused is significant

indicators.note: the letters of the three words are confused into a new order

parts.note: the letters of these words are used as written, as the fodder

explanation.surface: Someone wonders why their confusion matters so much.
explanation.definitionFit: A weighty matter is important or serious, a synonym of significant.

clue.text: Weak player has rook and bishop captured by a piece

parts.note: R is the chess notation for a rook

indicators.note: the bishop letter is captured inside the other letters

parts.note: taken as written, the letter itself
a bit is a piece
B is the chess notation for a bishop

explanation.surface: A poor chess player loses rook and bishop to a single piece.
explanation.walkthrough: The chess setting is all surface; a rabbit is a sporting term for a poor player, especially in cricket or tennis.
explanation.definitionFit: Rabbit is informal for an inept player, a weak performer in a game.

clue.text: A competitor initially duplicated entry

parts.note: taken as written
a rival is a competitor, and its first letter is written twice

explanation.surface: A competitor's opening entry appears twice by mistake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Initially duplicated' means the competitor's first letter appears twice, so an extra R stands before it.
explanation.definitionFit: An arrival is a coming in, an entry onto a scene.

clue.text: Complete classical quartet turned up in house

indicators.note: in a down clue the letters read upwards, reversed

parts.note: all means complete or entire
IV is four in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: A full classical string quartet arrives at someone's house.
explanation.definitionFit: A villa is a large country or holiday house.

clue.text: Went on rampage with tirade about carnival scene

indicators.note: the tirade surrounds the carnival city

parts.note: a rant is a tirade
Rio de Janeiro is famous for its carnival

explanation.surface: A crowd at a carnival goes wild, shouting a tirade.
explanation.definitionFit: To run riot is an idiom for behaving in a wild and uncontrolled way.

clue.text: Excellent fish found in British stream

parts.note: a rill is a small stream

explanation.surface: A fine fish is caught in a British brook.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Excellent' is also a second meaning: brill is British slang for brilliant.
explanation.definitionFit: Brill is a European flatfish related to the turbot.

clue.text: Enclose page by court official for clerk

indicators.note: the court official is placed by, right after, the enclosing word and the page letter

parts.note: to pen is to shut in
an usher keeps order in a law court

explanation.surface: A court official is told to confine a page boy, alongside the clerk.
explanation.definitionFit: A pen-pusher is a disparaging name for a clerk or office worker doing routine paperwork.

clue.text: Generate changes for young person

indicators.note: the letters of the first word undergo changes into a new order

parts.note: the letters of this word are used as written, as the fodder

explanation.surface: Bring about changes for the benefit of youth.
explanation.definitionFit: A teenager is someone aged thirteen to nineteen, so a young person.

clue.text: Scot's understanding no backward African

parts.note: ken is Scots for knowledge or understanding

indicators.note: the word for no is read in reverse

parts.note: nay is an old word for no

explanation.surface: A Scotsman's grasp of things is not behind that of an African.
explanation.definitionFit: A Kenyan is a person from Kenya in East Africa.
